text: How many months are in one year of the Gregorian calendar?
explanation: A Gregorian year has twelve calendar months.

text: How many sides does a triangle have?
explanation: A triangle is a polygon with three sides.

text: What is half of 100?
explanation: Dividing 100 by two gives 50.

text: How many items make one dozen?
explanation: A dozen is a group of twelve.

text: What do the letters UN stand for?
explanation: The United Nations is an international organization.

text: How many official languages does the United Nations have?
explanation: The six are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.

text: What is the sum of the interior angles of a Euclidean triangle?
explanation: The three interior angles of a plane triangle add to 180 degrees.

text: Which SI prefix means one thousand?
explanation: The prefix kilo denotes a factor of 10 to the third power.

text: A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its area?
explanation: The area of a square is side length multiplied by itself.

text: What is the probability of heads on one fair coin toss?
explanation: There are two equally likely outcomes and one is heads.

text: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability of a total of 2?
explanation: Only the pair 1 and 1 works among 36 equally likely pairs.

text: What is the median of 2, 5, 9, 11 and 20?
explanation: The median is the middle value in an ordered data set.

text: Which number is prime?
explanation: The only positive divisors of 29 are 1 and 29.

text: A right triangle has perpendicular sides 5 and 12. How long is its hypotenuse?
explanation: The Pythagorean theorem gives the square root of 25 plus 144.

text: How many different orders can four distinct books have on a shelf?
explanation: There are 4 times 3 times 2 times 1 possible orders.

text: Which SI base unit measures luminous intensity?
explanation: The candela is the SI base unit for luminous intensity.

text: Which SI base unit measures amount of substance?
explanation: Amount of substance is measured in moles.

text: Which defining constant is used in the modern SI definition of the kilogram?
explanation: The kilogram definition fixes the numerical value of the Planck constant.

text: Which SI prefix represents a factor of 10 to the power minus 9?
explanation: Nano denotes one billionth of the base unit.

text: Which SI base unit measures thermodynamic temperature?
explanation: Thermodynamic temperature has the SI base unit kelvin.

text: What is the chemical symbol for hydrogen?
explanation: Hydrogen has the symbol H and atomic number 1.

text: Which element has the symbol O?
explanation: O is the symbol for oxygen.

text: Which element has the symbol C?
explanation: Carbon is element 6, represented by C.

text: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
explanation: Sodium has the symbol Na.

text: Which element has the symbol Fe?
explanation: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron.

text: Which organelle is a major site of aerobic ATP production in eukaryotic cells?
explanation: Cellular respiration produces ATP in mitochondria.

text: Which organelle carries out photosynthesis in plants?
explanation: Chloroplasts contain the photosynthetic machinery.

text: Which DNA base pairs with adenine in the standard double helix?
explanation: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

text: Which structure contains most of a eukaryotic cell's DNA?
explanation: Most eukaryotic DNA is housed in the nucleus.

text: Which gas is released by oxygenic photosynthesis?
explanation: Oxygenic photosynthesis releases oxygen from water.

text: In F = ma, what does a represent?
explanation: Newton's second law relates net force to mass and acceleration.

text: What is the exact speed of light in vacuum in metres per second?
explanation: The SI fixes this value exactly at 299792458 metres per second.

text: At approximately 1 atmosphere, what is the freezing point of pure water?
explanation: At normal atmospheric pressure pure water freezes near zero Celsius.

text: What determines an element's atomic number?
explanation: Each element is defined by its proton count.

text: What electric charge does a proton have?
explanation: Protons carry positive elementary charge.

text: Which element has the symbol Au?
explanation: Au is the symbol for gold.

text: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
explanation: Potassium has the symbol K.

text: Which element has the symbol W?
explanation: W represents tungsten, historically called wolfram.

text: Which metal is liquid at 20 degrees Celsius and normal pressure?
explanation: Mercury melts well below room temperature.

text: Which nonmetal is liquid at 20 degrees Celsius and normal pressure?
explanation: Bromine is liquid at room temperature.

text: In what year did the United Nations come into existence?
explanation: The UN Charter entered into force on 24 October 1945.

text: In what year was the US Declaration of Independence adopted?
explanation: Congress adopted the Declaration on 4 July 1776.

text: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?
explanation: The Giza pyramids are royal monuments of ancient Egypt.

text: Which country contains the historic Great Wall?
explanation: The Great Wall is a historic defensive system in China.

text: Which city was divided by the Berlin Wall?
explanation: The Wall divided Berlin from 1961 to 1989.

text: In what year did the Berlin Wall open?
explanation: Border crossings opened on 9 November 1989.

text: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
explanation: Machu Picchu was built during the Inca Empire.

text: Petra was a major capital of which ancient people?
explanation: Petra was the Nabataean capital and a trading center.

text: Angkor was a center of which empire?
explanation: Angkor preserves monuments of the Khmer Empire.

text: In what year was the US Constitution signed?
explanation: The Constitution was signed on 17 September 1787.

text: In which city was the United Nations Charter signed in 1945?
explanation: The Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

text: How many countries were original members of the United Nations?
explanation: The UN began with 51 original member states.

text: Which English king agreed to Magna Carta in 1215?
explanation: King John agreed to Magna Carta in June 1215.

text: Which document formed the first constitution of the United States?
explanation: The Articles of Confederation preceded the present Constitution.

text: What year is associated with the US Emancipation Proclamation taking effect?
explanation: Lincoln's proclamation took effect on 1 January 1863.

text: Which pharaoh is associated with the Great Pyramid at Giza?
explanation: The Great Pyramid was built for Khufu.

text: Which ancient Egyptian capital appears in the UNESCO site name with its necropolis and Giza pyramids?
explanation: The World Heritage property is Memphis and its Necropolis.

text: Which court's statute forms an integral part of the UN Charter?
explanation: The ICJ Statute is annexed to the UN Charter.

text: Which century saw the construction of Machu Picchu?
explanation: Machu Picchu was built in the fifteenth century.

text: The Magna Carta displayed at the US National Archives dates from which year?
explanation: The Archives displays Edward I's 1297 reissue.

text: Which ocean is the largest by area?
explanation: The Pacific is Earth's largest ocean basin.

text: Which continent has the largest land area?
explanation: Asia is the largest continent.

text: Which line marks zero degrees latitude?
explanation: The Equator is the reference line for latitude.

text: What is the capital of Japan?
explanation: Tokyo is Japan's capital.

text: What is the capital of Pakistan?
explanation: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan.

text: Which mountain has the highest summit above sea level?
explanation: Everest has the highest elevation above mean sea level.

text: Which continent has no permanent native human population?
explanation: Antarctica has research stations but no indigenous permanent population.

text: What is the capital of Canada?
explanation: Ottawa is Canada's national capital.

text: Which Russian lake is the world's deepest lake?
explanation: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth.

text: Which mountain range runs along western South America?
explanation: The Andes extend along South America's western edge.

text: Which strait connects the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea?
explanation: Gibraltar separates southern Spain from northern Morocco.

text: Which meridian is the conventional reference for zero degrees longitude?
explanation: Longitude is measured east or west of the prime meridian.

text: Which ocean contains Challenger Deep?
explanation: Challenger Deep is in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific.

text: What is the capital of Mongolia?
explanation: Ulaanbaatar is Mongolia's capital.

text: Which hemisphere contains a place at 35 degrees south latitude?
explanation: South latitude places a location south of the Equator.

text: The International Date Line roughly follows which longitude?
explanation: The Date Line broadly follows the 180-degree meridian.

text: How many arcminutes make one degree of latitude?
explanation: A degree is divided into 60 minutes of arc.

text: At which latitude do all meridians meet at the North Pole?
explanation: The North Pole is at 90 degrees north latitude.

text: A location has coordinates 20 degrees N, 70 degrees E. Which pair of hemispheres contains it?
explanation: N indicates north of the Equator and E indicates east longitude.

text: Which World Heritage lake contains about one fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water?
explanation: UNESCO describes Baikal as holding about 20 percent of unfrozen freshwater reserves.

text: Which language gives web pages their basic document structure?
explanation: HTML is a markup language used to structure web documents.

text: What is CSS primarily used for on the web?
explanation: CSS controls the presentation of structured documents.

text: Who invented the World Wide Web?
explanation: Berners-Lee invented the Web at CERN in 1989.

text: How many bits are in a conventional byte?
explanation: A byte conventionally contains eight bits.

text: What does URL stand for?
explanation: A URL identifies the location of a resource.

text: Which two digits are used in binary notation?
explanation: Base-two notation uses just zero and one.

text: What is hexadecimal 0x10 in decimal?
explanation: The first place beyond the units in base sixteen has value sixteen.

text: What does HTTP status code 404 mean?
explanation: 404 indicates that the target resource was not found.

text: Which service translates domain names into records such as IP addresses?
explanation: The Domain Name System maps names to resource records.

text: Which format uses object members written as name/value pairs?
explanation: JSON represents structured data with objects and arrays.

text: How many bits long is an IPv6 address?
explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long.

text: Which HTTP method requests a representation of a resource?
explanation: GET requests transfer of a current representation of the target resource.

text: What does a SQL PRIMARY KEY identify?
explanation: A primary key identifies rows in a table.

text: Which SQL clause filters rows according to a condition?
explanation: WHERE specifies the row selection condition.

text: Which HTTP status code indicates successful creation of a resource?
explanation: 201 Created reports that the request created one or more resources.

text: How many bytes can one Unicode scalar value occupy in UTF-8?
explanation: UTF-8 uses sequences of one through four bytes.

text: Which HTTP method has the same semantics as GET but sends no response content?
explanation: HEAD requests headers without transferring the representation content.

text: What is the maximum numeric value of an unsigned 8-bit integer?
explanation: Eight bits allow 256 values, numbered zero through 255.

text: In database transactions, what does the A in ACID mean?
explanation: Atomicity means a transaction's changes occur as one unit.

text: Which JSON literal represents the deliberate absence of a value?
explanation: JSON defines the literal null; undefined is not a JSON value.

text: In association football, how many players does a team normally have on the field, including the goalkeeper?
explanation: The Laws of the Game specify a maximum of eleven players per team.

text: How many legal deliveries make an over in cricket?
explanation: An over contains six valid balls; wides and no-balls do not count.

text: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
explanation: A shuttle is used in badminton.

text: In tennis scoring, what does love mean?
explanation: Love denotes a score of zero.

text: How many rings are in the Olympic symbol?
explanation: The Olympic symbol consists of five interlaced rings.

text: What is the standard marathon distance?
explanation: The marathon is run over 42.195 kilometres.

text: How many stumps form one cricket wicket?
explanation: A wicket comprises three stumps with two bails on top.

text: How long is a standard association football match, excluding added time?
explanation: A match has two equal halves of 45 minutes.

text: How many points is a successful free throw worth in FIBA basketball?
explanation: A free throw scores one point.

text: What is a 40-all score called in tennis?
explanation: At 40-all the score is deuce.

text: How long is a cricket pitch between the wickets?
explanation: The pitch is 22 yards long.

text: How far is the penalty mark from the goal line in association football?
explanation: The penalty mark is eleven metres from the midpoint between the posts.

text: How many events make up the athletics decathlon?
explanation: The decathlon combines ten track and field events.

text: Which athletics race includes a water jump and barriers?
explanation: The steeplechase combines barriers with a water jump.

text: How many players are on court for each team in standard FIBA five-on-five basketball?
explanation: Five players from each team are on the playing court.

text: What is the minimum number of players a football team needs for a match to start or continue?
explanation: A match may not start or continue with fewer than seven players on a team.

text: What is the width of a cricket wicket?
explanation: The three stumps form a wicket nine inches wide.

text: In association football, can a player be offside when receiving the ball directly from a throw-in?
explanation: There is no offside offence when receiving directly from a throw-in.

text: Under standard advantage scoring in tennis, how many consecutive points from deuce win a game?
explanation: A player must win the advantage point and then the next point.

text: How many barriers and water jumps in total are cleared in a standard 3000-metre steeplechase?
explanation: The race has 28 hurdle jumps and seven water jumps.

text: Which Pixar film features Woody and Buzz Lightyear?
explanation: Woody and Buzz are the central toy characters in Toy Story.

text: What kind of fish is Nemo in Finding Nemo?
explanation: Nemo and his father Marlin are clownfish.

text: Which Pixar film follows the emotions inside Riley's mind?
explanation: Inside Out personifies Riley's emotions.

text: Which film features the monster duo Mike and Sulley?
explanation: Mike Wazowski and James P. Sullivan work at Monsters, Inc.

text: Which Cars character is a racing car?
explanation: Lightning McQueen is the red racing car at the center of Cars.

text: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Picture, then called Outstanding Picture?
explanation: Wings received the award at the first Oscar ceremony.

text: Which film won the first Oscar for Animated Feature?
explanation: Shrek won the inaugural Animated Feature award in 2002.

text: Who directed Titanic, the 1997 feature film?
explanation: Cameron won the directing Oscar for Titanic.

text: Who directed Spirited Away?
explanation: Miyazaki directed the 2003 Animated Feature Oscar winner.

text: Who directed The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King?
explanation: Peter Jackson won the directing Oscar for the film.

text: In which year was Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs first released?
explanation: Disney's first full-length animated feature premiered in 1937.

text: Which film won Best Picture at the 1998 Academy Awards?
explanation: Titanic won Best Picture at the 70th Academy Awards.

text: Which film won Animated Feature at the 2004 Academy Awards?
explanation: Finding Nemo won the 2004 Animated Feature Oscar.

text: How many Oscars did The Return of the King win at the 2004 ceremony?
explanation: It won all eleven categories in which it was nominated.

text: What is the Oscar statuette's official name?
explanation: The Academy Award of Merit is commonly called the Oscar.

text: Who won the first Academy Award for Actor?
explanation: Jannings won for The Last Command and The Way of All Flesh.

text: Who won the first Academy Award for Actress?
explanation: Gaynor received the first Actress Oscar for three performances.

text: In which Los Angeles hotel was the first Academy Awards ceremony held?
explanation: The first ceremony was held in the Roosevelt's Blossom Room.

text: Who designed the original Oscar statuette figure?
explanation: MGM art director Cedric Gibbons designed the statuette.

text: What were Oscar statuettes made of during three years of World War II?
explanation: A wartime metal shortage led to painted plaster Oscars.

text: How many lines are in a standard musical staff?
explanation: A standard staff has five lines and four spaces.

text: Which clef is also called the G clef?
explanation: The treble clef identifies the G line.

text: What does tempo describe?
explanation: Tempo describes how fast or slowly the beat moves.

text: What does the dynamic marking f mean?
explanation: F stands for forte, meaning loud.

text: How many beats does a quarter note receive in 4/4 time?
explanation: In 4/4 the quarter note is the beat unit.

text: Which clef is also called the F clef?
explanation: The bass clef identifies the F line.

text: What does a crescendo indicate?
explanation: Crescendo calls for a gradual increase in loudness.

text: How many semitones make one octave in twelve-tone equal temperament?
explanation: An octave spans twelve equal semitone steps.

text: Which tempo term usually means fast and lively?
explanation: Allegro is a fast tempo marking.

text: How many notes make up a triad?
explanation: A triad contains a root, a third and a fifth.

text: What is the interval from C up to G in the same octave?
explanation: C to G spans a perfect fifth.

text: How many sharps or flats are in the key signature of C major?
explanation: C major uses no sharps or flats in its key signature.

text: What is the relative minor of C major?
explanation: A natural minor shares C major's key signature.

text: Which scale raises both its sixth and seventh degrees when ascending in the traditional form?
explanation: Traditional melodic minor raises degrees six and seven ascending.

text: What interval separates the root and third of a minor triad?
explanation: A minor triad has a minor third above the root.

text: What interval is the inversion of a major third?
explanation: Inverted interval sizes add to nine, and major becomes minor.

text: How many semitones span an augmented fourth?
explanation: An augmented fourth is a tritone of six semitones.

text: Which notes form a C diminished triad?
explanation: A diminished triad combines two minor thirds.

text: Which major key has four sharps in its key signature?
explanation: E major has F-sharp, C-sharp, G-sharp and D-sharp.

text: Which scale degree is called the dominant?
explanation: The dominant is the fifth scale degree.

text: Who wrote Pride and Prejudice?
explanation: Pride and Prejudice is a novel by Jane Austen.

text: Who wrote Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus?
explanation: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein.

text: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
explanation: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy by Shakespeare.

text: Who wrote A Tale of Two Cities?
explanation: Dickens wrote the novel set in London and Paris.

text: Who wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
explanation: Lewis Carroll is the pen name used by Charles Dodgson.

text: Which detective lives at 221B Baker Street in Arthur Conan Doyle's stories?
explanation: Holmes shares the Baker Street lodgings with Dr Watson.

text: What is the surname of the five sisters in Pride and Prejudice?
explanation: The novel follows the Bennet family.

text: Who is the captain of the Pequod in Moby-Dick?
explanation: Captain Ahab pursues the white whale.

text: In Dracula, what is Count Dracula?
explanation: Stoker's Count Dracula is a vampire.

text: Which novel features the orphan Pip?
explanation: Pip is the narrator of Great Expectations.

text: Who wrote The Picture of Dorian Gray?
explanation: Wilde's novel centers on Dorian Gray and his portrait.

text: Who wrote The Time Machine?
explanation: Wells published The Time Machine in 1895.

text: Who wrote The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde?
explanation: Stevenson wrote the novella about Jekyll and Hyde.

text: Who wrote Wuthering Heights?
explanation: Wuthering Heights is Emily Bronte's novel.

text: Who wrote Middlemarch?
explanation: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans.

text: What is the name of the scientist who creates the creature in Frankenstein?
explanation: Victor Frankenstein creates the unnamed creature.

text: Which Shakespeare play features the magician Prospero?
explanation: Prospero is the exiled duke and magician in The Tempest.

text: What is the name of the ship in Treasure Island?
explanation: The Hispaniola carries the treasure-seeking expedition.

text: Which novel features Dorothea Brooke?
explanation: Dorothea Brooke is a central character in Middlemarch.

text: Who narrates the opening of Moby-Dick with the words Call me Ishmael?
explanation: Ishmael is the novel's first-person narrator.

text: What makes up most of a giant panda's diet?
explanation: Giant pandas feed chiefly on bamboo.

text: Which animal is the fastest land mammal?
explanation: Cheetahs are specialized for short bursts of high-speed running.

text: Which land animal is the tallest?
explanation: Giraffes are the tallest living land animals.

text: Which group do penguins belong to?
explanation: Penguins are flightless marine birds.

text: How many arms does an octopus have?
explanation: An octopus has eight arms.

text: Which mammal lays eggs?
explanation: The platypus is an egg-laying monotreme.

text: Which leaves make up most of a koala's diet?
explanation: Koalas mainly eat eucalyptus leaves.

text: Which fish is the largest living fish species?
explanation: Whale sharks are the largest living fish.

text: Which mammals are capable of sustained powered flight?
explanation: Bats are the only mammals with true powered flight.

text: Which animal group undergoes a caterpillar stage?
explanation: A caterpillar is the larval stage of a butterfly.

text: What gives flamingos their pink coloration?
explanation: Dietary carotenoids contribute to flamingos' pink plumage.

text: Which living mammal uses a bill to detect prey's electrical signals?
explanation: The platypus detects weak electric fields with receptors in its bill.

text: How many hearts does a giant Pacific octopus have?
explanation: Two hearts serve the gills and one serves the rest of the body.

text: A koala is classified as which type of mammal?
explanation: Koalas are marsupials that rear young in a pouch.

text: What term describes the transfer of pollen by bees between flowers?
explanation: Bees carry pollen while visiting flowers.

text: Which amphibian is known for retaining external gills as an adult?
explanation: Axolotls retain larval features including external gills.

text: Which natural lake system in Mexico is the axolotl's remaining native stronghold?
explanation: Wild axolotls are native to the Xochimilco water system.

text: What name is often given to the giant panda's enlarged wrist bone used to grasp bamboo?
explanation: An enlarged wrist bone functions like an opposable thumb.

text: What is the scientific name of the cheetah?
explanation: The cheetah belongs to the genus Acinonyx.

text: Which tusk-bearing elephant species typically has smaller ears than African savanna elephants?
explanation: Asian elephants generally have smaller ears than African elephants.

text: Which legume is used to make traditional tofu?
explanation: Tofu is made from coagulated soy milk.

text: Sushi rice is traditionally seasoned with which acidic ingredient?
explanation: Sushi uses rice seasoned with vinegar, commonly rice vinegar.

text: Which spice is made from dried flower stigmas?
explanation: Saffron comes from the stigmas of Crocus sativus.

text: Which plant part is cinnamon traditionally made from?
explanation: Cinnamon is obtained from the inner bark of certain trees.

text: Which fruit is the main ingredient in guacamole?
explanation: Guacamole is an avocado-based preparation.

text: What kind of organism makes bread dough rise in ordinary yeast bread?
explanation: Yeast ferments sugars and produces carbon dioxide.

text: Which legume is the main ingredient in traditional hummus?
explanation: Hummus is commonly made with chickpeas and tahini.

text: Tahini is a paste made primarily from which seeds?
explanation: Tahini is ground sesame seed paste.

text: Cocoa powder is made from the seeds of which tree?
explanation: Cocoa is produced from cacao beans.

text: Which vitamin is citrus fruit particularly known for supplying?
explanation: Citrus fruits are well-known dietary sources of vitamin C.

text: Which protein network gives wheat dough much of its elasticity?
explanation: Hydrated wheat proteins form gluten in dough.

text: Which Japanese seasoning paste is traditionally made by fermenting soybeans with salt and koji?
explanation: Miso is a fermented soybean seasoning.

text: Which aromatic spice consists of dried flower buds?
explanation: Cloves are the dried unopened buds of the clove tree.

text: Which plant part is ginger commonly used as a spice?
explanation: Culinary ginger is an underground stem called a rhizome.

text: Which process turns milk into yogurt using bacterial cultures?
explanation: Yogurt cultures ferment milk sugars into lactic acid.

text: Quinoa is botanically best described as what type of food crop?
explanation: Quinoa is not a grass, but its seeds are used like cereal grains.

text: Which compound is chiefly responsible for the heat of chili peppers?
explanation: Capsaicin activates heat-sensitive receptors.

text: Which spice comes from the aril around a nutmeg seed?
explanation: Mace is the dried aril; nutmeg is the seed.

text: Which preparation is added to milk in traditional cheese making to coagulate casein?
explanation: Rennet enzymes coagulate milk proteins into curds.

text: Which reaction between reducing sugars and amino compounds produces much of the browning in cooked food?
explanation: The Maillard reaction creates many browned colors and aromas.

text: How many planets are in our solar system?
explanation: The solar system has eight recognized planets.

text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
explanation: Mercury is the innermost planet.

text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
explanation: Iron minerals give Mars its reddish appearance.

text: Which planet is the largest in the solar system?
explanation: Jupiter is the solar system's largest planet.

text: What is Earth's natural satellite called?
explanation: Earth has one natural moon.

text: Which planet has the hottest average surface among the eight planets?
explanation: Venus's dense atmosphere traps heat efficiently.

text: Which two planets have no natural moons?
explanation: Mercury and Venus have no natural moons.

text: Between which two planets is the main asteroid belt?
explanation: The main asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

text: Which planet is farthest from the Sun among the eight planets?
explanation: Neptune is the outermost of the eight planets.

text: What is Pluto classified as?
explanation: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt.

text: Which planet has an axial tilt of about 98 degrees and rotates nearly on its side?
explanation: Uranus's extreme axial tilt makes its rotation unusual.

text: What is the name of Jupiter's largest moon?
explanation: Ganymede is also the largest moon in the solar system.

text: Which spacecraft mission studied Saturn from orbit for more than a decade?
explanation: Cassini orbited Saturn from 2004 until 2017.

text: Which Apollo mission first landed humans on the Moon?
explanation: Apollo 11 landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin in 1969.

text: Which Martian moons are named after fear and panic?
explanation: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

text: Which Jovian moon is the most volcanically active world in the solar system?
explanation: Io's intense volcanic activity is driven by tidal heating.

text: Which large moon has its own internally generated magnetic field?
explanation: Ganymede is the only known moon with its own intrinsic magnetic field.

text: Which moon's icy surface overlies a likely global ocean and is a target for Europa Clipper?
explanation: Europa has strong evidence for a subsurface saltwater ocean.

text: What is the approximate orbital period of Neptune in Earth years?
explanation: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun.

text: What is the name of Pluto's largest moon?
explanation: Charon is unusually large relative to Pluto.
